per_depth.common_affordance: Because each rule couples only a pair of switches, a failing condition on one side forces the other side's condition to hold — the rules propagate as chains of forced consequences. Engineers sometimes fear this needs exhaustive search, but the pairwise structure makes the consequences fully deducible.
The explicit clause-by-clause framing where each requirement is presented as a disjunction of two signed literals (exact textbook 2-SAT formulation).
direct 2-SAT clause framing (satisfying at least one literal per pair of signed indices)
The explicit implication phrasing ('if opposite, requires expected') directly handing models the directed edges of the 2-SAT implication graph
The explicit factored zero-product equation $(s_{|l_1|} - t(l_1)) \times (s_{|l_2|} - t(l_2)) = 0$ mapping 1-to-1 to a 2-SAT clause
direct 1-to-1 correspondence with DIMACS CNF 2-SAT literal pairs
The direct pairwise mutual exclusion condition (NOT (A and B)) over binary variables, directly defining 2-SAT.
The explicit definition of phase index as $(-1)^{s + \delta}$ and condition $P(l_1) + P(l_2) \le 0$, which cleanly isolates each detector to a single 2-SAT clause forbidding $(1, 1)$.
The direct equivalence between a detector remaining dormant and a standard 2-variable disjunction (v1 OR v2), mapping 1-to-1 to 2-SAT with DIMACS-signed literals.
The explicit rule that a brace fails only when both endpoints contract (-2 mm), which trivially unpacks into a 2-CNF clause per brace.
